properties.chose:
@ajs, 2026-10-17, after proof-trial rung 2 (fact:the-proof-trial-rung-2-ran-on-flo2-io-and-what-counts-holds-while-recording-a-proof-is-still-costly-2026-10-17), where about 19 creates were refused, some across types and some between two statements of the same proof. He chose:
- Cross-type: "Note, never refuse" (option (a)). The hand-kept PRESCRIBED_LAYER_PAIRS list gives way to a rule.
- Within a proof: "Note, never refuse". A same-type near-match between reasoning records (a statement carrying a statement_kind, or an Inference) is reported on the successful write.
- Every other same-type near-match keeps today's refusal.
Options (b) and (c) are not chosen. The recorded counter-argument, a cross-layer restatement now gets a note rather than a stop, was weighed and accepted: the note and the read-back still show it. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the dev_storyflow agent's 2026-09-24 entry (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27), written after add_capability was refused over a dated finding. In the reporter's words: "Opportunity: cross-type near-matches as a note on success rather than a refusal, keeping refusal for same-type matches."

WHAT EXISTS TODAY. 14 cross-type pairs already behave exactly this way: PRESCRIBED_LAYER_PAIRS in capture.rs, where the match comes back in search_first.near_matches on a write that succeeded. Every OTHER cross-type pair refuses. Measured on 0.72.0 (fact:root-cause-a-dated-finding-blocks-four-intent-constructors-because-an-unlisted-cross-type-pair-refuses-2026-09-28): one TemporalFact refuses add_capability, add_requirement, add_design_rule and add_component, and is only a note for add_decision.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORTER'S. Every cross-type near-match is a note on success, and only a same-type match refuses. This replaces the list with a rule. Cheap: one filter in the shared refuse_unless_deliberate, and the near-match report survives unchanged.
(b) A NARROWER RULE. An OBSERVATION record (TemporalFact, ChangeEvent, Verification) never refuses an INTENT write, while intent↔intent cross-type pairs stay on the list. That answers this report's class (a dated record against intent) without reopening the intent-layer pairs.
(c) KEEP THE LIST and add TemporalFact↔{Capability, Requirement, DesignRule, Component} on today's evidence. This is the path taken four times already (08-31, 09-01, 09-05, 09-16).

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT EACH (findings, not a ranking). (a) and (b) are stated rules, so a class test can pin them. (c) cannot be pinned as a class, because it is a list. The 2026-09-16 root cause called (c) "a hand-maintained allowlist standing in for a rule the design already states". (b) keeps a catch for an agent restating a Requirement as a Capability-shaped DesignRule, for example; (a) does not.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-17: every cross-type near-match is a note on a successful write (option a), and a near-match between two records of a line of reasoning is a note too; the same-type refusal stays for everything else
properties.rationale:
THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than against it. chg:a-cross-type-near-match-is-named-as-a-layer considered option (a) on 2026-08-29 and REJECTED it: "Excluding cross-type pairs from the filter would have removed the friction and also removed a real catch when an agent genuinely duplicates an idea across layers — trading a false alarm for a silent miss." The refusal's own text still says a node that only restates another "can wear a different type". The 19/0 non-duplicate count comes from agents grading their own writes, so it is a lower bound on the false-positive rate, not a proven zero, and nobody has audited it.

AGAINST THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: the list has had to grow for field reports five times. bhome showed agents pre-empting with distinct_from on every write, which is the silent miss arriving by another route and leaving no record. The refusal's own first sentence concedes the hit is "not a near-duplicate". And a TemporalFact is a dated observation, so an intent node can never be the same record written twice.

WHOSE IDEA: the dev_storyflow project's agent session (relayed in the field report), triaged for who:ajs.
